mutants.mutation: os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent, follow_symlinks=False) -> os.stat(name, dir_fd=None, follow_symlinks=False) in ResourceGuard.write_bound absent-branch appeared-target guard
mutants.evidence: Differential check: with the stat guard made blind to dir_fd (equivalent to dir_fd=None), write_bound on a target that appears after binding raises ResourceError('write target appeared after authorization') identically to pristine. The os.open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL, dir_fd=parent) backstop fails closed on the already-present target, so dropping dir_fd from the advisory stat cannot let an appeared target be written.
mutants.verification: current 406-test suite: all 18 write_bound-mapped tests pass under the mutant (8 directly re-run, plus full mutmut fresh run 3011/3313)

mutants.mutation: os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent, follow_symlinks=False) -> os.stat(name, follow_symlinks=False) in ResourceGuard.write_bound absent-branch appeared-target guard
mutants.evidence: Same as mutmut_69: removing the dir_fd argument leaves the advisory stat resolving against the process CWD instead of the target parent directory, but the subsequent os.open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL, dir_fd=parent) fails closed with ResourceError when the target appeared after binding. Behaviorally identical rejection on all reachable inputs.
mutants.verification: current 406-test suite: all 18 write_bound-mapped tests pass under the mutant (8 directly re-run, plus full mutmut fresh run 3011/3313)
